mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry or Chamber of Commerce of the corporate partner's country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the country of residence or the competent issuing public authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letters and Source of Wealth / Source of Funds declarations for each UBO contributing initial assets (issued less than 3 months before filing)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-registry authority or an accredited LEI Local Operating Unit

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all General Partners, Limited Partners (when natural persons), UBOs, authorised signatories and trading representatives against: (i) PEP status (domestic and foreign political exposure); (ii) the EU Council consolidated financial sanctions list; (iii) UN Security Council sanctions, including ISIL/Al-Qaida resolutions; (iv) OFAC SDN list including the 50% ownership rule; and (v) Luxembourg domestic asset-freeze measures coordinated by the Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is triggered by PEP status, FATF-listed high-risk third countries, unusual geographic patterns, or opaque ownership structures. Any suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing gives rise to an immediate report to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier) under the amended Law of 12 November 2004. Data must be retained for at least 5 years after the end of the business relationship, per CSSF AML/CFT requirements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) electronic portal at www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The chosen name must begin or end with the abbreviation 'SCSp' or the full expression 'Société en commandite spéciale' (Article 1465-11 of the Law of 10 August 1915). Names are filed and displayed in Latin script; administrative filings are made in French or German, and any English-language constitutional document must be accompanied by a certified French translation for RCS publication. If the intended commercial name uses non-Latin script, a single verified transliteration must be used consistently in the partnership agreement, RCS filing and marketing materials. The name must not be misleading, contrary to public order or decency, or create confusion with an existing registered Luxembourg company or a protected trademark.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, Bank, Banquier (requires prior CSSF banking license)
Assurance, Insurance, Réassurance (requires prior Commissariat aux Assurances authorization)
SICAV, FCP, FIS, SIF, OPCVM, fonds d'investissement (collective investment undertakings requiring CSSF regulatory status)
Luxembourg, État, National, Gouvernement (any wording implying State or public authority connection)
Fiduciaire, Trust, Société de fiducie (regulated fiduciary activities)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The initial RCS name reservation is valid for 30 days and may be renewed by written application to the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) before expiry, with successive renewals permitted subject to LBR fees where the incorporation is delayed by KYC, apostille or partner-signature steps. Upon a name rejection, the applicant may first file a reasoned reconsideration request with the LBR within 15 days of the refusal notice; if the refusal is maintained, the applicant may bring an administrative appeal before the Luxembourg Tribunal administratif within 3 months of notification of the final decision. Alternatively, the applicant may withdraw the rejected name and immediately submit a new reservation application. Where the rejection is grounded on a third-party trademark conflict, an express written consent or trademark coexistence agreement can be filed to secure re-admission of the name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Luxembourg-registered office is a legal requirement for the SCSp; the registered office may be supplied by an authorised professional domiciliation agent (agréé), which is a standard and acceptable solution for a low-risk app-growth agency. However, a purely virtual address without any operational substance, management oversight, document retention or decision-taking capacity in Luxembourg exposes the entity to ACD tax-residency challenges, RBE/OECD BEPS Action 5 substance scrutiny and banking onboarding refusals. For this agency, professional domiciliation plus a Luxembourg resident manager or an appointed local administrative agent is the minimum recommended commercial-substance configuration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 15% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first fiscal year. LBR/RBE compliance verification, the Luxembourg direct tax administration (Administration des Contributions Directes) and the VAT administration (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA) may all conduct on-site checks. The likelihood increases materially if the registered office is a high-density domiciliation cluster with no personnel, no client-facing activity evidence and no local documentation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (previously Luxembourg Companies Law), Title VI bis – Société en Commandite Spéciale, Articles 907-1 to 907-9; general provisions of Articles 1 and 180-182.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Deed of Company / Partnership Agreement (Contrat de Société) – filed electronically with the RCSL
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is imposed on an SCSp. Capital is fixed freely in the partnership agreement and may be contributed in cash or in kind. No escrow account is required by law, though bank practice may require a capital account for opening operational accounts.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the SCSp is constituted under Luxembourg law with initial partnership interests subscribed as set forth in the Partnership Agreement; that the registered office of the SCSp is hereby established at [Address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; that [Name] is appointed as the Manager and authorised signatory of the SCSp, empowered to represent the partnership, open and operate bank and payment-agent accounts, and instruct counsel; that this Manager is further authorised to file the partnership deed, to register the SCSp with the Luxembourg Business Registers, to cause publication in the Mémorial C, and to take all steps necessary to commence the activity of app store optimization and multilingual SEO services in accordance with the objects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary in Luxembourg or private deed with certified signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Luxembourg-law partnership agreement containing the SCSp's name, registered office, corporate purpose, contribution amounts, classes of partnership interests, identity of the general partner, manager's powers, and tax pass-through election. Execute as a notarial deed or by private act before a Luxembourg notary or with authenticated signatures to satisfy bank and registration requirements.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of all partners and the general partner
Proof of address of each partner
Declaration of contributions and schedule of capital
Power of attorney if signed by representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or any partner rejects a clause, the document is revised by legal counsel and re-executed; no formal adverse Registry action applies at this drafting stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission to the Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the LBR eRegistry with authenticated credentials or use the notary's direct transmission. File the executed partnership agreement, statutory forms, and supporting declarations. Pay the prescribed RCSL registration fee online. Obtain a filing receipt with an electronic acknowledgment reference.
required_dossiers: Form C (request for registration of a company)
Identification documents of the general partner and manager
Declaration of compliance with AML/CFT obligations (L. 12 November 2004)
Proof of registered office address (lease agreement or letter of address)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCSL issues a query or incompleteness notice, the applicant must correct the dossier or submit a legal rebuttal within 15 working days; failure to cure may result in rejection with right to resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Examination and Registration in the RCSL
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCSL registration desk (Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCSL validates legal form, corporate purpose, general partner capacity, and conformity with the Law of 10 August 1915. Upon approval, the SCSp receives a Luxembourg RCSL identification number (B/E number) and its registration is entered in the official register.
required_dossiers: Original notarial deed or private deed with certified signatures
List of general partners and their capacity details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is refused, the applicant may apply to the District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) for a review within one month of notification; legal counsel will assist in preparing the court application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Official Electronic Compendium (Mémorial C)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Official Electronic Compendium of Companies and Associations (ROJG – Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCSL registration, the LBR automatically transmits the legal notice to the Mémorial C. The publication includes the SCSp's name, registered office, corporate object, general partner details, and registration number. No separate applicant action is required; the notice is published online.
required_dossiers: No additional submission – published ex officio from RCSL registration data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication contains material errors, the applicant must file a written rectification request with the RCSL, identifying the inaccurate field and supplying the correct data; the Registry will issue a corrected publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax, VAT and Social Security Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (Luxembourg Tax Administration) and Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Luxembourg business identification number (matricule) and VAT number, if applicable, through the tax office or via the RCSL registration data. Register the general partner with the CCSS for social security status. Optionally verify whether an establishment authorisation is required with the Ministry of the Economy – for this non-regulated digital services activity, no authorisation is mandatory.
required_dossiers: RCSL registration certificate (extract of the register)
Passport and identity documents of the general partner and manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed, the applicant or authorised professional may escalate to the relevant tax office by written request; for VAT delays, contact the Administration de l'enregistrement et des domaines (AED) if invoicing is needed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Direction Générale des Classes Moyennes (only for optional establishment authorisations; not required for non-regulated professional services under ISIC 7310)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory industry-specific operating licence applies to app store optimization, multilingual SEO localization, and digital marketing agency services in Luxembourg.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement – Environmental Protection Agency, Luxembourg
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category Exempt – No EIA required for office-based service activity; the activity generates no industrial pollutants or environmental risks.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A – no wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams; general waste disposal obligations under the Luxembourg Waste Law (Loi du 21 mars 2012) apply only to ordinary office waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance is required for the registered office under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 July 1985 on fire safety, and workplace inspection clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) is mandatory for employee health and safety compliance. Structural load certifications are not required for standard office floors. Employers must also register with the CCSS and submit workplace rules as applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT — portal: guichet.lu and MyGuichet electronic filing services
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity that carries out taxable supplies in Luxembourg must register with AEDT for a Luxembourg VAT identification number (often combined with a national business number). The application is filed electronically through MyGuichet using the registration form for non-established taxable persons, accompanied by proof of foreign registration, constitutional documents, identity documents of directors/managers, and a summary of intended activities. The AEDT assigns a 9-digit national registration number enabling VAT submission and customs interaction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is fiscally transparent by default for Luxembourg income tax and net wealth tax purposes; no check-the-box election exists under domestic law. For VAT, the SCSp is treated as a taxable person where it independently supplies goods or services, and it may apply the VAT grouping election under Article 61 of the VAT Law with AEDT authorization. Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD apply to negative tax transparency mismatches, and no election to become opaque is generally available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold for non-established suppliers making first taxable supply in Luxembourg; small domestic businesses may benefit from the EUR 35,000 annual turnover exemption. For cross-border distance sales, the EU-wide EUR 10,000 threshold applies before Luxembourg VAT registration is required unless the OSS scheme is used.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, an API clearance mandate, or digital stamping regime is in force. Electronic invoices are accepted if kept in their original electronic format and considered authentic and legible, preferably conforming to the European standard EN 16931. Invoices must be transmitted with the recipient's consent, and all invoices, including e-invoice audit files, must be retained and produced to AEDT upon demand.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods to a destination outside the EU qualifies for the 0% rate if the goods are physically dispatched or transported out of the EU by the supplier, a customer not established in Luxembourg, or a third party acting for them, within the statutory proof period. Exported services (e.g., ASO/localization services) supplied to a non-EU taxable person or to a non-EU private person with effective use and enjoyment outside Luxembourg may be zero-rated or outside scope, subject to showing the service recipient's non-EU status and the actual export nature of the transaction.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT authorities may verify export proofs retrospectively, and if the supplier cannot demonstrate timely and legal export, the zero rating is disallowed and the VAT becomes payable, with potential recovery (clawback) of input VAT previously deducted. Fraudulent attempts to obtain an unwarranted zero rating trigger VAT evasion penalties ranging from a civil fine of up to EUR 250,000, recovery of unpaid tax plus interest, and criminal prosecution with up to five years' imprisonment for commercial fraud. AEDT applies strict documentary completeness and chain-of-custody checks before approving any export refund claim.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem framework and in coordination with the European Central Bank (ECB); exchange control and capital movement supervision is harmonised at EU level, with the CSSF responsible for credit institution prudential oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies full current and capital account convertibility under EU Treaty provisions (Articles 63-66 TFEU) and the EU Capital Movements Directive. No exchange control authorisation is required for current payments, profit remittances, repatriation of capital, or foreign direct investment flows. Profit remittance by a Luxembourg SCSp to non-resident partners is unrestricted, subject only to standard tax reporting and anti-money laundering verification; no 'profit remittance tax' or balance-of-payments approval applies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion requirements in Luxembourg or in the eurozone. Export receipts may be held freely in EUR or any other currency, credited to designated foreign currency accounts, and used for legitimate commercial purposes without requiring BCL approval. Luxembourg imposes no forex retention or repatriation deadline on a SCSp's export earnings.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
BGL BNP Paribas Luxembourg (now BNP Paribas Fortis Luxembourg)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for a non-bank payment institution registered in Luxembourg or an EU-licensed e-money institution passported into Luxembourg (e.g., Wise B2B, Payoneer EU) to service the SCSp. Cross-border fintech EMIs are permitted to hold client funds, conduct FX conversions, and execute SEPA and international payments without a domestic banking licence. However, such EMIs generally cannot provide credit, commercial letter of credit issuance, or guaranteed clearing services; for escrow-grade capital subscriptions and shareholder loan disbursements, a Tier-1 credit institution account remains the mandatory anchor. Legal constraint: an SCSp is not a financial sector professional, so no CSSF licence is required, but the EMI must comply with GDPR, AML/CFT, and payment services rules in the country of account establishment.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively required for first-time board members and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) when opening a corporate bank account with major Luxembourg banks. Remote signing and video-interview onboarding are possible for established shareholders or additional signatories, but the general manager and at least one authorised partner of the SCSp must normally appear in person at the bank's Luxembourg branch or at a recognised foreign correspondent branch for the initial KYC session. Banks may waive physical presence only where the SCSp has a pre-existing relationship with the same banking group and where biometric verification through a trusted third party is available; for a de novo SCSp, a physical interview is the prudent assumption.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of initial capital from non-resident partners resident in higher-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised partnership agreement; certificate of registration from the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS); bank and brokerage statements showing the origin of each partner's funds; prior-year audited financial statements or tax returns of the partners; explanation of the commercial substance of the SEO/localisation agency; signed declarations of the UBOs with names, citizenship, and proof of address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments to third-party SEO platforms and contractors with no obvious relation to registered activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed client contracts and subcontractor agreements detailing the scope of app-store optimisation services; detailed invoice register with amounts, dates, and purpose of each payment; evidence of actual service delivery (reports, screenshots, performance dashboards); logical explanation of the commercial rationale linked to ISIC 7310; any intellectual property licence if software payments are involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency incoming transfers from multiple jurisdictions with no consistent counterparty profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customer due diligence file on all recurring clients, including corporate registration certificates, UBO registries, and sanction-screening results; an existing marketing and sales pipeline underlying the payment flow; clear segregation of client funds from operating funds; monthly reconciliation reports prepared by an independent Luxembourg accountant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Partner distributions or shareholder loan repayments within a short period after capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substance documentation proving that the SCSp is not a flow-through shell; board minutes and capital call notices explaining the timing of distributions; tax estimates prepared by a Luxembourg tax adviser confirming that the distribution is consistent with partnership pass-through treatment; bank statements evidencing the availability of audited profits or cash from ongoing operations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital for the SCSp must be routed via SWIFT MT103 or SEPA immediate credit transfer from the partner's account to the SCSp's dedicated capital escrow account at a Luxembourg Tier-1 bank. Remitters must state a precise payment purpose code, generally 'P001' (positive income) or 'P002' (capital and reserve) under the EU Balance of Payments classification, with the reference line 'SCSp capital contribution under partnership agreement dated [date]'. The receiving bank will verify the identity of the remitter against the RCS UBO register and may request the capital call notice; the funds must be booked as partnership equity, not as debt, unless a formal shareholder loan agreement exists. For amounts exceeding EUR 10,000, an automatic CSSF/AML reporting threshold triggers, requiring comprehensive source-of-funds documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for app-store optimisation, multilingual search services, and performance marketing purchases are cleared via (i) SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR payments within the EEA, (ii) SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA and foreign-currency payments, and (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit where the counterparty requires documentary credit security, particularly for large programmematic advertising purchases. Disbursement instructions must match the invoice and the underlying contract; purpose codes such as 'P030' (services) or 'P050' (royalties and licence fees) are used according to the actual service. For contractor payments in USD/GBP/CHF, the bank executes a spot conversion at the fix, or the SCSp can pre-fund a foreign currency account via a forward hedge.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards with a Luxembourg credit institution for USD, GBP, CHF, and JPY exposures, underlying commercial invoices only
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) via authorised EU banks for currencies of targeted app-store jurisdictions without full onshore market access, subject to CSSF suitability
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for matching expected USD/EUR advertising spend against revenue earned in Baltics or CEEMEA markets
FX spot contracts for immediate trade settlements and working capital conversions
Vanilla FX options for managing downside risk on large outbound licensing fees, subject to position limits agreed with the bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS data confirmation (déclaration annuelle au Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), filing via the e-justice portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each calendar year by 31 December; confirmation window runs from 1 January to 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: LBR issues a formal reminder after the deadline; continued non-confirmation blocks issuance of RCS extracts and good-standing certificates and may trigger a fine of EUR 150 to EUR 5,000 and eventual administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once per calendar year, no later than 31 December; event-driven updates within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines of EUR 500 to EUR 1,250 for natural persons and EUR 1,000 to EUR 25,000 for legal persons for omitted or incorrect UBO data; false declarations may also give rise to imprisonment and delisting risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (full or abridged) with the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RCS via e-justice electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the end of the financial year; 31 July for a calendar-year-end SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered coercive fine (astreinte) obtainable by the Public Prosecutor or any interested party; fine of EUR 150 to EUR 5,000 under the Law of 19 December 2002; persistent non-filing leads to administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual tax transparency return (allocation of taxable result to partners)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) / Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 December of the year following the taxable year; extended deadlines available when filed electronically by an approved tax professional
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of assessed tax (minimum EUR 100), late-payment interest of 0.6% per month, and risk of ex officio assessment of allocable income at partner level.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory Luxembourg audit (contrôle légal) applies when the SCSp exceeds at least two of three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average headcount 50. A réviseur d'entreprises agréé must then be appointed. Below these thresholds, no compulsory statutory audit applies to the SCSp.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial companies and accounting (implementing EU Directive 2013/34/EU) and the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies; IFRS-EU is permitted for supervised or specially regulated investment structures.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must maintain accurate beneficial-ownership data in the RBE and confirm it electronically at least once per calendar year by 31 December. Any transfer of partnership interests or change in the ultimate ownership chain must be reported to the RBE within 30 days of the change; the annual confirmation is a verification refresh and does not replace event-driven UBO filings.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book
